rfi.description: Two Namibian colonial-era political prisoners, whose remains were returned by South Africa last week, are to be reburied in Namibia as part of Wednesday’s Heroes Day ceremonies. They are among a group of Namibians who died in South Africa under apartheid or during the colonial period and whose remains have been repatriated.

rfi.title: France says US risks ‘blocking everything’ at UN talks to protect world’s soils
rfi.description: The soil that grows the world's food and holds its water is becoming less productive, yet governments are struggling to agree on how to respond to this crisis. As political talks at Cop17, the United Nations conference on desertification and land degradation, stepped up in Mongolia on Tuesday, France's environment ambassador Barbara Pompili warned that disputes involving the United States are threatening progress.

rfi.title: France's Sophie Adenot returns to the void for second spacewalk in a week
rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot on Tuesday stepped outside the International Space Station (ISS) for the second time, a week after she became the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Adenot and US astronaut Anil Menon are due to finish replacing a faulty antenna on the ISS after running out of time during their first spacewalk on 18 August.

rfi.title: Looking up: French radio enthusiast captures ISS signals from his garage
rfi.description: Astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. In the second episode of a five-part series, RFI hears from Vincent Plousey, a radio ham from Tavaux in eastern France whose hobby is picking up signals from the ISS using homemade antennas built in his garage.

rfi.title: Survivors of Guinea's deadly landfill collapse say authorities ignored warnings
rfi.description: Two days after a deadly landfill collapse in Guinea, rescuers are using giant excavators to search for victims. Anger is rising among residents, who say they had warned authorities that the rubbish dump was precarious.

rfi.title: US and Denmark push for nationwide expansion of UN arms embargo in Sudan
rfi.description: The United States on Monday urged the United Nations Security Council to expand an arms embargo on the Sudanese region of Darfur to cover all of Sudan, saying the nation's brutal conflict risks regional expansion. The suggestion was supported by Denmark, which holds the Council's rotating presidency.

rfi.title: At least 40 killed as gangs attack displaced people near Haiti capital

rfi.title: French village reels from tornado that damaged hundreds of homes
rfi.description: Hundreds of damaged homes, widespread power cuts and blocked roads confronted residents of southwestern France on Tuesday after a tornado tore through the village of Pomas, injuring 39 people, two of them critically.

rfi.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean

rfi.title: Ukraine's allies pledge to continue support with focus on air defence

france24fr.description: 🇬🇳 En Guinée, la solidarité s’organise après l’éboulement meurtrier d’une décharge qui a fait 31 morts dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche. Plusieurs centaines d’habitants ont été évacués vers une école transformée en centre d’hébergement temporaire.

france24fr.title: La légende de la country Dolly Parton est morte à 80 ans
france24fr.description: La légende américaine de la country Dolly Parton est morte à 80 ans. De "Jolene" à "I Will Always Love You", l'autrice de quelque 3 000 chansons laisse une empreinte majeure sur la culture populaire américaine. Sa famille n'a pas précisé la cause de sa mort.

france24fr.title: Après un Mondial 2026 réussi, le Marocain Bouaddi file à Manchester City pour un montant record
france24fr.description: Rayonnant à Lille depuis deux saisons et avec le Maroc lors du Mondial 2026, Ayyoub Bouaddi s'est engagé avec Manchester City, mercredi, jusqu'en 2031. Les Citizens ont déboursé pas moins de 100 millions d'euros pour s'attacher les services du jeunes milieu de terrain de 18 ans, un montant record.

france24fr.title: Soudan : les États-Unis veulent étendre l’embargo sur les armes
france24fr.description: Les Etats-Unis ont proposé lundi d'étendre à tout le Soudan, en guerre depuis plus de trois ans, l'embargo des Nations unies sur les armes instauré au Darfour, pour faire face au risque de régionalisation du conflit.

france24fr.title: Tchad : l’extraction de sable menace le fleuve Chari
france24fr.description: Au Tchad, l’extraction de sable dans des carrières qui longent le fleuve Chari met en péril le cours d’eau et l’environnement alentour. C’est pour cette raison que le ministère des Mines a interdit cette activité. Mais cette décision ne plaît pas à tout le monde.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : à Gorée, immersion dans le très sélectif lycée Mariama Bâ
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, découverte de l’École Mariama Bâ, située sur l’île de Gorée, au large de Dakar. Cet établissement réservé aux filles accueille, après un concours très sélectif, des élèves venues de tout le pays. L’école a notamment pour objectif de leur donner les moyens de s’affirmer et de développer leurs compétences.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RD Congo : pourquoi la riposte peine-t-elle à contenir l'épidémie ?
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, la propagation de l'épidémie d’Ebola est plus rapide que la riposte … C’est le constat alarmant des acteurs humanitaires présents dans les zones touchées par le virus. Selon l’OMS, une personne meurt d’Ebola toutes les 30 minutes. Il s’agit de l’épidémie la plus meurtrière de l’histoire du pays. Pourquoi la riposte peine-t-elle à contenir l’épidémie ? Les précisions d'Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula, correpondante France 24 à Kinshasa.

france24fr.title: Syrie : les FDS dissoutes, qui sont ces forces kurdes ?
france24fr.description: Le chef kurde syrien Mazloum Abdi a annoncé mardi soir la dissolution des Forces démocratiques syriennes, les FDS. Une décision prise dans le cadre de l’accord conclu avec le président syrien Ahmad al-Chareh, qui prévoit leur intégration aux institutions de l’État syrien. Mais qui sont ces forces kurdes ? Les explicatiosn de Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international à France 24.

france24fr.title: Pakistan : 14 nourrissons tués dans l'incendie d'un service de maternité
france24fr.description: Un incendie qui s'est déclaré mercredi dans le service de maternité d'un hôpital d'Islamabad a coûté la vie à 14 nourrissons, ont indiqué les autorités pakistanaises, qui ont attribué le sinistre à un climatiseur défectueux.

france24fr.title: Le Kremlin confirme la visite du directeur de la CIA mais dément une rencontre avec Poutine
france24fr.description: Le directeur de la CIA, John Ratcliffe, s'est rendu mardi à Moscou pour échanger "entre services secrets", sans rencontrer le président Vladimir Poutine, a affirmé mercredi le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov.

france24fr.title: Droits de douane : le Canada durcit sa riposte face aux États-Unis
france24fr.description: Le Canada imposera à partir du 8 septembre des droits de douane de 15 à 50% sur une série de produits américains et ripostera encore si son secteur automobile est touché par de nouvelles surtaxes des Etats-Unis, avec qui la guerre commerciale s'envenime. Les précisions de Serge Jaumain, professeur d'histoire contemporaine à l'ULB.

france24fr.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude : l'IA peut-elle être raciste ?
france24fr.description: Une intelligence artificielle peut-elle reproduire des préjugés racistes ? C’est la question posée après un test mené par des internautes sur . À une même phrase, ses réponses peuvent varier selon la nationalité de la personne évoquée : avec un Italien, elle suggère parfois de parler gastronomie, tandis qu’avec un Algérien, elle peut aller jusqu’à conseiller d’appeler la police. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Afghanistan : un million d’enfants menacés par la malnutrition, alerte l’Unicef
france24fr.description: Un million d'enfants souffrant de malnutrition aigüe sévère en Afghanistan se trouvent en danger de mort si rien n'est fait pour leur venir en aide, a prévenu mardi le Fonds des Nations unies pour l'enfance (Unicef).

france24fr.title: Inondations meurtrières au Népal, de "nombreuses victimes" au Tibet
france24fr.description: Des torrents d'eau boueuse ont fait au moins 19 morts mercredi au Népal tandis que 384 touristes sont portés disparus. De "nombreuses victimes" sont recensées de l'autre côté de la frontière avec la Chine, au Tibet, selon les médias d'État chinois.

france24fr.title: Le Canada riposte en imposant des surtaxes de 15 à 50% aux Etats-Unis
france24fr.description: Le Canada imposera à partir du 8 septembre des droits de douane de 15 à 50% sur une série de produits américains et ripostera encore si son secteur automobile est touché par de nouvelles surtaxes des Etats-Unis, avec qui la guerre commerciale s'envenime.

france24fr.title: France : Pomas, village des Corbières, dévasté par une tornade
france24fr.description: Au lendemain du passage d'une tornade d'une violence exceptionnelle, les habitants de Pomas (Aude), traumatisés, évaluent l'ampleur des dégâts : 300 maisons sur 500 ont été endommagées, mais le bilan humain reste limité à une cinquantaine de blessés.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : la Cour suprême donne gain de cause à Trump sur le vote par correspondance
france24fr.description: La Cour suprême des Etats-Unis a ⁠levé lundi une injonction qui ​empêchait l'administration du président Donald Trump de mettre en oeuvre un décret prévoyant des restrictions sur le vote par correspondance en vue des élections de mi-mandat au Congrès ​américain en novembre prochain (les "midterms").

france24fr.title: Méditerranée : le poisson-baliste gagne du terrain et inquiète les baigneurs
france24fr.description: Le réchauffement de la Méditerranée favorise l’arrivée de nouvelles espèces dans ses eaux. Parmi elles, le poisson-baliste, dont la présence se multiplie près des côtes et qui peut mordre les baigneurs lorsqu’il protège son nid.

zeit.title: Neue Bachlinien und Lager: Millionen-Projekt: Großbäckerei Bonback in Halle wächst
3. Fußball-Liga: Auch Abwehrspieler Aidonis verlängert in Aspach
Literatur: Ungarischer Schriftsteller Peter Nadas stirbt mit 83 Jahren
Landtagswahl: So wählen blinde und sehbehinderte Menschen
Karikaturist: »Titanic«-Mitgründer Hans Traxler gestorben
zeit.description: Mit der »Neuen Frankfurter Schule« prägte Hans Traxler die Satire-Kunst der Bundesrepublik. Im Alter von 97 Jahren starb er in Frankfurt.

zeit.title: Nachtarbeiten diese Woche: Arbeiten an Saalebrücken - Das müssen Anwohner wissen
Eine Stadt sieht rot: Austoben bei der Tomatenschlacht in Spanien
Windenergie: Stromerzeugung aus Wind hat in Brandenburg stark zugelegt
Digitalverband Bitkom: Deutsche Firmen erleben häufiger Angriffe ausländischer Geheimdienste
zeit.description: Fast alle deutschen Unternehmen registrieren Fälle von Datendiebstahl, Industriespionage oder Sabotage. In vielen Fällen gehen sie von ausländischen Geheimdiensten aus.

zeit.title: VW-Betriebsversammlungen: VW will Management um ein Viertel verkleinern
zeit.description: In mehreren VW-Werken fürchten die Angestellten um ihre Jobs. Im Werk Emden sprach Oliver Blume über Einsparungen: Auch im Management soll es Einschnitte geben.

zeit.title: Ferat Koçak: Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt gegen Linken-Abgeordneten
zeit.description: Gegen den Abgeordneten Ferat Koçak laufen Ermittlungen wegen Verdachts auf Urkundenfälschung. Es geht um eine falsche Zugangskarte, die offenbar als Scherz gedacht war.

zeit.title: Nepal: Hunderte vermisste Touristen nach Sturzflut in Nepal
zeit.description: Nach einer schweren Sturzflut in Nepal werden mindestens 384 Reisende vermisst, darunter 291 Ausländer. Die Behörden meldeten bisher neun Tote und große Sachschäden.

zeit.title: Masernimpfungen: Arzt wegen Ausstellung Hunderter falscher Impfnachweise angeklagt
zeit.description: Ein Arzt aus Bayern soll mehr als 1.300 falsche Nachweise über Masernimpfungen ausgestellt haben. Die Generalstaatsanwaltschaft Nürnberg erhob nun Anklage gegen ihn.

zeit.title: Kabinettsklausur: Friedrich Merz hält an Abschaffung von Rente mit 63 fest
zeit.description: Der Kanzler will die Rentenreform wie geplant umsetzen – trotz Kritik der ostdeutschen CDU-Regierungschefs. Die Bevölkerung ruft er zu mehr Zuversicht auf.

observador.title: Bill Gates. IA deve ser "prioridade número um do mundo"
observador.description: Despedimentos massivos e fortunas trilionárias. As reflexões do fundador da Microsoft sobre o desenvolvimento acelerado da IA, que merece toda a atenção dos líderes mundiais.

observador.title: Os casos Luís Neves e os bastidores das polícias — Debate
observador.description: PJ, PSP, GNR, ASAE, Guardas Prisionais, Polícias Municipais... como são escrutinadas estas forças de autoridade? E há mesmo uma guerra entre polícias? Afinal o que se passa com as polícias?

observador.title: Harry e Meghan chegaram ao Reino Unido esta quarta-feira
observador.description: Os duques de Sussex terão viajado num jato privado, vindos da Califórnia, e devem instalar-se numa residência privada na região de Cotswolds. Archie e Lilibet começam o ano letivo na próxima semana

observador.title: Arábia Saudita recusa aderir aos Acordos de Abraão
observador.description: A Arábia Saudita admite aderir aos acordos, mas com uma condição: a adesão só será formalizada se for estabelecido o Estado da Palestina. Ainda, Netanyahu apelida iranianos de "selvagens".

observador.title: CIP quer que reforma das pensões avance "já" e "sem truques"
observador.description: Armindo Monteiro pede aos partidos que não percam tempo apenas para fixarem "clientelas eleitorais". E apela a que Governo não coloque reflexão sobre sistema de pensões na gaveta.

observador.title: Planos da RTP com saída de 157 trabalhadores autorizados
observador.description: O Governo deu luz verde aos planos da RTP para atividade e orçamento de 2026, que apontam à saída de 157 trabalhadores. No entanto, quer que RTP vá mais longe e sinaliza que vai manter valor da CAV.

observador.title: Albufeira. Ferido oriundo do Norte transferido para o Porto
observador.description: Um dos feridos graves na sequência do atropelamento em Albufeira, oriundo do norte, vai ser transferido para o Hospital de São João, no Porto. O outro ferido grave fica no Hospital de Portimão.

observador.title: Tom Holland em Portugal: família, golfe e Zendaya
observador.description: O ator revelou que já em criança passava férias por cá, onde volta sempre para jogar golfe. Celebrou os anos na Comporta a comer "frango piri piri" e regressou a Lisboa esta semana com a mulher.

observador.title: 12h. Chega não retira projeto sobre identidade de género
observador.description: Em causa os projetos de lei do PSD, Chega e CDS, que preveem obrigatoriedade de validação médica para mudança de nome e género. Ainda, diretor da CIA pode ter visitado Moscovo no dia de ontem.

observador.title: Lisboa: Festas da Rua levam música e cinema a vários lugares
observador.description: A abertura do cartaz está marcada para o Vale do Silêncio, nos Olivais com a atuação das Divas Pop. Estarão presentes Cuca Roseta, Iolanda e Mimicat, numa noite que promete reviver memórias.

observador.title: Israel. Netanyahu chama "selvagens" aos líderes iranianos
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro israelita afirmou que é impossível chegar a acordo com os líderes iranianos, chamando.lheos chamado de "selvagens". Netanyahu garantiu retaliar com mais força do que nunca.

observador.title: Vila Real. Câmara destaca barro e andor da Senhora da Pena
observador.description: A Câmara de Vila Real visa promover a conservação do barro preto de Bisalhães, património da UNESCO, e do andor da Senhora da Pena através de workshops, exposições e outras atividades.

observador.title: Cinco semanas e meia depois, Palhinha cumpriu o seu destino
observador.description: Sporting deixou de ser opção no final de junho, clubes ingleses caíram como opção em julho, Benfica tornou-se o caminho inevitável em agosto: João Palhinha assina pelos encarnados por 14+5 milhões.

observador.title: Chega recusa retirar iniciativa após apelo da ONU
observador.description: A ONU manifestou-se contra a iniciativa do Chega, indicando que põe em causa direitos humanos e tratados internacionais e criticando a designação atribuída pelo partido de "transtorno".

observador.title: Moçambique aposta na IA mas alerta para perigo nas eleições
observador.description: A primeira-ministra moçambicana enumerou os pontos onde a Inteligência artificial pode apoiar os processos eleitorais, mas alertou que essas tecnologias podem "fragilizar" o processo.

observador.title: Banhos desaconselhados em Vila Praia de Âncora
observador.description: O município anunciou que estão desaconselhados os banhos na Vila Praia de Âncora. Uma das possíveis causas é o aumento do escoamento superficial provocado pelo mau tempo sentido nos últimos dias.

observador.title: Açores. Governo vai adquirir mais dois robôs cirúrgicos
observador.description: O concurso está avaliado em 3,8 milhões de euros e visa a aquisição de equipamento de cirurgia robótica e uma mesa operatória para a Ilha Terceira e de equipamento cirúrgico de ortopedia para a Horta.

observador.title: INE. Avaliação bancária da habitação bate um novo recorde
observador.description: No mês de julho foi atingido o novo máximo histórico de 2.240 euros por metro quadrado, um aumento de 12 euros face a junho, mais 15,2% em comparação ao período homólogo de 2025.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Bund führt biometrische Identitätskarte ein +++ Bundesrat beschleunigt Einführung von Cell Broadcast
Im Sommer 1991 wird ein belgischer Sozialistenführer ermordet – dann bringt die mysteriöse Affäre den Nato-Generalsekretär zu Fall
nzz.description: Er sagte von sich, schon vor der Geburt Sozialist gewesen zu sein: André Cools wurde vor 35 Jahren kaltblütig ermordet. Bis heute ist der Fall nicht restlos aufgeklärt. Doch die Ermittlungen brachten einen folgenschweren Korruptionsskandal zutage.

nzz.title: In den USA eskaliert der Konflikt zwischen Finanzminister und Notenbankchef: Nun ergreift eine «graue Eminenz» Partei gegen Bessent
nzz.description: Der Milliardär Stanley Druckenmiller kritisiert die Schuldenpolitik seines einstigen Zöglings, dem US-Finanzminister Scott Bessent. Er stellt sich damit auf die Seite von Fed-Chef Warsh.

nzz.title: Mindestens acht Tote und Hunderte von Vermissten nach Sturzflut an Grenze zwischen China und Nepal
nzz.description: Eine Sturzflut ergiesst sich unvermittelt durch das Hochland im Himalaja. An der Grenze zwischen China und Nepal kommen Menschen zu Tode. Unklar bleibt jedoch, was die Schlammmassen losbrechen liess.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Kultur: Oesch’s die Dritten kündigen Abschiedstournee an
Waldbrandgefahr, aber kaum Löschflugzeuge: Deutschland setzt auf australische Restbestände
nzz.description: Transall waren früher Transportflugzeuge der deutschen Bundeswehr. Nun werden ausgemusterte Exemplare zu Löschflugzeugen umgerüstet – auch für Einsätze in Deutschland.

nzz.title: Aryna Sabalenka ist die Weltnummer eins im Tennis, doch seit Monaten verliert sie nur noch. Was ist passiert?
nzz.description: Am US Open könnte die Weissrussin ihre monatelange Baisse beenden. Doch dafür muss sie ihre mentale Stärke wiederfinden.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Klimaforscher warnt vor mehr Extremwetter +++ Hunderte Menschen in Spanien wegen Waldbrand evakuiert
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen zum Hitzesommer in Europa.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Umbruch bei VW: Heiss soll laut Medienbericht auf Wiegend im Aufsichtsrat folgen +++ Volkswagen-Chef Oliver Blume betont die Notwendigkeit der Sparmassnahmen
nzz.description: Der VW-Chef Oliver Blume will den Konzern radikal umbauen, um ihn zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Belegschaft äussert bei den angelaufenen Betriebsversammlungen Kritik. Anfang September dürften erste Entscheide getroffen werden.

nzz.title: Nach Enthüllungen wegen Polizeiaffäre: Die Stadt Uster entzieht der zuständigen Stadträtin das Dossier
nzz.description: Die GLP-Politikerin Beatrice Caviezel war an der Manipulation von Rechnungen beteiligt. Dazu kam eine Affäre um anonyme Schmähbriefe. Nun soll es eine externe Untersuchung geben.

nzz.title: Geheimnisvolle Reise von John Ratcliffe: Warum war der CIA-Chef in Moskau?
nzz.description: Der Chef des amerikanischen Auslandgeheimdiensts war für einige Stunden in der russischen Hauptstadt. Zur Reise gibt es kaum bestätigte Informationen, aber viele offene Fragen.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: Der Krieg in der Ukraine franst aus – und die Gefahr einer militärischen Eskalation zwischen Russland und der Nato wächst
nzz.description: Russische Drohnen und Marschflugkörper gelangen immer häufiger in Nato-Gebiet. Aus der Reaktion der Allianz kann Moskau viel lernen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: SpaceX will 100 Milliarden Dollar in neuen Weltraumbahnhof stecken +++ Raiffeisen baut trotz Gewinnsprung bis zu 180 Stellen ab
Handelskonflikt USA-Kanada: Widerstand und Stolz der Kanadier
nzz.description: Die amerikanischen Strafzölle haben für kanadische Unternehmen verheerende Folgen. Dennoch steht die Bevölkerung hinter dem Kurs der Regierung. Eine Kleinunternehmerin, ein Lokalpolitiker und ein Möbelfabrikant erzählen.

spiegel.title: AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt: Warum Migranten aus Angst vor Siegmund streiken
spiegel.description: Dutzende Migranten wollen ihre Geschäfte schließen, um vor einer AfD-Regierung in Sachsen-Anhalt zu warnen. Drei von ihnen erzählen von der Angst vor Rassismus, Sorgen um ihre Kinder – und der Hoffnung, doch noch etwas zu bewegen.

spiegel.title: Goch: Gefundene Patrone explodiert in Hand – 16-Jähriger verletzt
spiegel.description: Mit einem Metalldetektor hat ein Jugendlicher ein Feld in Nordrhein-Westfalen abgesucht. Er fand alte Munition und hob sie auf. Doch die Patrone war noch explosiv.

spiegel.title: Zuckersteuer: Vizekanzler Klingbeil vollzieht Kehrtwende bei Zero-Getränken
spiegel.description: Lars Klingbeil muss bei der Zuckersteuer zurückrudern: Getränke mit Süstoffen sollen nun doch nicht mit einer Abgabe belegt werden. Wie das passieren konnte und was der Finanzminister sonst noch zurückziehen musste.

spiegel.title: Fußball-Transfers: João Palhinha kehrt nach Lissabon zurück – Wechsel perfekt
spiegel.description: João Palhinha wechselt aus München nach Lissabon. Leverkusen holt offenbar Moussa Diaby zurück. Und Manchester City zahlt 100 Millionen Euro für einen potenziellen Rodri-Nachfolger. Transfers und Gerüchte im Überblick.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Gewerkschaft der Polizei: Warum GdP-Vize Sven Hüber kurz vor dem Abschied hinschmeißt
spiegel.description: GdP-Vize Sven Hüber sieht sich nach einer scharfen Attacke gegen die AfD mit neuen Vorwürfen aus seiner Zeit als DDR-Grenzer konfrontiert. Nun schmeißt er kurz vor seinem Abschied hin. Er spricht von »Rufmord«.

spiegel.title: Die Linke: Ferat Koçak bastelt einen Bundestags-Ausweis – und hat mächtig Ärger
spiegel.description: Die Berliner Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt gegen den Linkenabgeordneten Ferat Koçak wegen Urkundenfälschung. Tatsächlich hat er einen falschen Bundestagsausweis hergestellt. Hier erklärt er, warum.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz wirbt für Aufbruchsstimmung in Deutschland – und Ende des »Missmuts«
spiegel.description: Zum Ende des Kabinettstreffens in Brandenburg beschwören Union und SPD eine gute Zukunft für Deutschland. Kanzler Merz will ein Ende der Verdrießlichkeit – und stellt sich gegen die Rentenwünsche der ostdeutschen Landeschefs.

spiegel.title: Dolly Parton ist tot: Bilder aus dem funkelnden Leben der Country-Ikone
spiegel.description: Ihre Songs gehören zu den erfolgreichsten der Welt, auf der Bühne glänzte sie mit ihrer Stimme und Strass. Doch Dolly Partons Strahlkraft ging noch über die Musik hinaus. Bilder eines einzigartigen Lebens.

spiegel.title: VW will Management um ein Viertel verkleinern
spiegel.description: Der Sparkurs bei VW trifft auch die Führungsetage. Betroffen sind hauptsächlich Verwaltung, Entwicklung und Vertrieb. Konzernchef Oliver Blume spricht von einem »gemeinsamen Kraftakt«.

spiegel.title: Nepal: Hunderte Einheimische und Touristen nach Sturzflut vermisst
spiegel.description: Eine Sturzflut im Himalaja hat ganze Dörfer weggespült, es gibt Berichte über Tote. Laut Tourismusbehörde werden zudem mindestens 384 Reisende vermisst.

spiegel.title: Belgien: Führt die Spur des Waldbrands Naturschutzgebiet Hohes Venn in die Landwirtschaft?
spiegel.description: Die belgischen Behörden äußern erstmals einen Verdacht, wie es zu der Brandkatastrophe im Osten des Landes kommen konnte. Die Feuerwehr kämpft derweil noch immer gegen Glutnester des Feuers mit historischem Ausmaß.

spiegel.title: Cornwall: Forschende zeichnen Todeskampf eines Wals im Stellnetz auf
spiegel.description: Ein Schweinswal suchte vor der Küste Großbritanniens nach Nahrung, als er sich in einem Stellnetz verfing. Was dann passierte, konnten Wissenschaftler durch Zufall detailliert nachvollziehen.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Kyjiw bemüht sich um Freigabe von Starlink – und verleiht Elon Musk höchsten Orden
spiegel.description: Bisher verweigert Elon Musk der Ukraine bei ihrem Abwehrkampf den Einsatz von Starlink-Internet auf russischem Staatsgebiet. Nun bekommt er den Orden der Freiheit von Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj verliehen.

spiegel.title: Koblenz: Staatsanwaltschaft fordert lebenslange Haft für mutmaßlichen Mörder von Amy Lopez
spiegel.description: 1994 wurde eine US-Touristin in Koblenz Opfer eines Gewaltverbrechens. 30 Jahre später soll ein 81-jähriger Mann für den Mord an der Frau verurteilt werden. Er hatte die Tat gestanden.

spiegel.title: Papst Leo XIV.: »Vanity Fair« nimmt ihn auf die Best-Dressed-Liste
spiegel.description: Die Hauptliste der bestangezogenen Menschen wird von Schauspielerinnen, Models und Sängern geprägt. Doch in einer Nebenkategorie hat das US-Magazin »Vanity Fair« auch Papst Leo XIV. für seinen Modegeschmack ausgezeichnet.

spiegel.title: Frankfurt am Main: Mitarbeiter des Flughafens an Malaria gestorben – fünf weitere infiziert
spiegel.description: Infektiöse Mücken sind offenbar im Flugzeug oder Gepäck bis zum Flughafen in Frankfurt am Main gelangt. Sechs Mitarbeiter erkrankten an Malaria, einer von ihnen starb. Nun sollen gefangene Mücken untersucht werden.

spiegel.title: Neuhardenberg: Das sagen Friedrich Merz, Lars Klingbeil und Alexander Dobrindt – Livestream

However, the LLM's implicit world model fails to learn the state of the LOB. This deficiency leads to biased estimates and spurious predictability in using the LLM to forecast future LOB events. Our analysis uses novel tests of an LLM's world model, extending prior work from deterministic settings

phys-org.title: Hyperdoped silicon photodiode advances short-wave infrared detection at room temperature
phys-org.description: Detecting short-wave infrared (SWIR) light, a region of the electromagnetic spectrum just beyond the light visible to the human eye, could be advantageous for many real-world applications. For instance, it could enable more advanced systems for capturing images at night, as well as sophisticated medical imaging, environmental monitoring and industrial inspection technologies.

phys-org.title: Appropriated racial oppression shapes Black parents' socialization of children
phys-org.description: Black parents who experienced higher levels of appropriated racial oppression—defined as shaping one's behavior and self-concept around dominant cultural norms of whiteness—were less likely to transmit positive, culturally protective messages that affirmed racial pride and self-worth to their adolescent children, a recent study found.

phys-org.title: Support groups for parents halved violence against children in wartime Ukraine, trial finds
phys-org.description: Ukrainian parents who joined a support group program called "Hope Groups," designed for families living through the war, reported that violence against children was cut in half and that they had less than half the depression and anxiety symptoms of parents who had not yet participated in the program, according to a new trial led by the University of Oxford.

phys-org.title: Researchers map tick habitat to strengthen African swine fever preparedness
phys-org.description: A small, nest-dwelling tick found across large parts of Texas could play an outsized role in how the United States responds to African swine fever (ASF) should the virus reach domestic or wild pigs.

phys-org.title: Utah mountain ranges may store a billion tons of hidden ice
phys-org.description: Unlike conventional glaciers, rock glaciers appear as piles of rock that obscure large masses of unaccounted-for ice. Rock glaciers are common in the Wasatch and Uinta ranges, even appearing on the Colorado Plateau in the La Sal Mountains near Moab.

phys-org.title: New quantum computing method broadens spectroscopy of hard-to-model matter
phys-org.description: Scientists could have a new way to explore the hidden behavior of matter, thanks to research involving Queen Mary University of London that uses a quantum computer to carry out a new form of computational spectroscopy.

phys-org.title: Butterfly-inspired crystals could enable durable, potentially safer glitter
phys-org.description: The next time you need to freshen up the paint on your house or apply a bit of cosmetic glitter before heading out for the night, you might want to give a quick nod to the butterflies fluttering in a nearby garden. Taking inspiration from structures on those wings that create their vibrant colors, researchers are now devising more durable and adjustable colors that are also safer for human health and the environment.

phys-org.title: Catalyzing the community: Chemists and Navajo leaders educate on clean water
phys-org.description: Many Native American communities in rural areas rely on well water, but the quality and safety of that water can vary significantly. Researchers led by Jani C. Ingram measured levels of heavy metals in well water on tribal lands through a community partnership with the Navajo Nation. After compiling their water-quality data, the researchers and tribal leaders developed best practices for distributing educational resources about safe drinking water to residents of Navajo reservations.

phys-org.title: Volcanic eruptions and warming climate disrupt long-standing link between Indian and Pacific oceans
phys-org.description: A new study that combines paleoclimate data and climate models suggests that large volcanic eruptions can disrupt the relationship between atmospheric circulation patterns over the tropical Indian and Pacific oceans. In addition, human-caused greenhouse gas emissions are now driving an unprecedented breakdown in interbasin coupling, according to researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI).

phys-org.title: Too small for fries: Drought shrinks Belgian potatoes
phys-org.description: Mathieu Comijn inspected rows of potatoes in a field of cracked earth and browned leaves, pulling from the ground tubers barely the size of pingpong balls.

phys-org.title: Fire haze threatens health of millions in Indonesia, ministry warns
phys-org.description: Millions of Indonesians risk health complications from exposure to thick haze covering several cities and towns, officials said Wednesday, as El Niño-fueled wildfires wreak havoc on Borneo and Sumatra.

phys-org.title: Plant-like chemical gardens show how simple reactions build complex structures
phys-org.description: The famous quote by Cicero, "If you have a garden and a library, you have everything you need," reminds us that the beauty of life lies in the harmony between nature and knowledge. More than 2,000 years later, this idea still resonates, particularly with a group of European researchers who have created a unique type of "garden": one that grows from chemistry itself.

phys-org.title: Even low-level traffic noise can reduce birdsong's stress-relieving effects
phys-org.description: Traffic noise disrupts recognized benefits of birdsong and other sounds from nature, a new study from the University of Surrey reports.

phys-org.title: Reusable stencils create clean carbon nanotube patterns in single-stage process
phys-org.description: Researchers from Skoltech and their colleagues from Harbin Institute of Technology in China and ITMO University in Russia have devised a way to deposit elaborate geometric patterns of carbon nanotubes without wasting material. Such patterns are used in advanced optical devices and mechanical strain sensors for structural integrity monitoring.

phys-org.title: From nuisance to new resource: Prickly pear could support fuels, foods and rural growers
phys-org.description: Texans often view prickly pear cactus as a nuisance, but researchers with Texas A&M AgriLife Research are seeking opportunity. Susanne Talcott, Ph.D., a molecular researcher and professor in the Texas A&M Department of Food Science and Technology, leads a multidisciplinary team studying how prickly pear cactus can serve as a source of biofuels and functional food ingredients.

phys-org.title: Finns may live to 80 or 85, but productive healthy years average 43 to 46
phys-org.description: For the first time in Finland, population-level norm values have been established for estimating life expectancy adjusted for health-related functional capacity and productivity. The new study provides Finnish norm values for both everyday functioning and work ability, as well as for a newly developed measure, productivity-adjusted life expectancy.

phys-org.title: Strong oyster reefs start with genetic diversity
phys-org.description: The European flat oyster (Ostrea edulis) was once widespread but has now become so scarce in the North Sea that it no longer forms ecologically functioning reefs. Along with the demise of the flat oyster, the three-dimensional structures that provide habitat for more than 100 marine species have disappeared. Restoration therefore focuses not only on the return of the European flat oyster itself but also on the reef and its associated biodiversity.

phys-org.title: Bright people know more about wine: How higher intelligence is reflected in deep domain knowledge
phys-org.description: Intelligent people tend to perform better at school and at work, as numerous studies have shown. But what happens in domains where incentives such as good grades or financial rewards don't apply and where socioeconomic status is not a significant factor? Wine knowledge is a case in point. Intelligence researcher Maximilian Krolo of Saarland University has investigated whether intelligence can predict the acquisition of deep knowledge in a specialized domain. undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Mess With Markets
proj-syn.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has justified his intervention in currency and bond markets by arguing that they are not providing a fair signal of economic fundamentals. But they are, and Bessent's willingness to peddle such nonsense may be the most striking testament yet to the sycophancy that defines the Trump administration.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh Owes Us an Apology
proj-syn.description: After only a few months in office, the chair of the US Federal Reserve has left market participants disoriented and confused. His first address to the annual monetary-policy symposium in Jackson Hole is an opportunity to set things aright—or to make matters even worse.

proj-syn.title: Is the Trump Treasury Panicking?
proj-syn.description: With the federal deficit near 6% of GDP and the national debt surpassing $40 trillion, America’s fiscal position looks increasingly precarious. By trying to strong-arm the bond market rather than address the underlying problem, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent may have squandered his hard-earned credibility.

proj-syn.title: What the World’s Oldest Bank Reveals About EU Financial Integration
proj-syn.description: To fend off an attempted takeover, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena has launched its own bids for two other Italian banks. The episode shows why EU policymakers should focus less on making governments surrender their influence over national banking systems and more on building a European financing channel.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
proj-syn.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still other

proj-syn.title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
proj-syn.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
proj-syn.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: China’s Platform State and the AI Race
proj-syn.description: Balancing regulation with innovation is never easy, and the Chinese government’s robust support for AI could lead to inefficiency and excess. But the “platform state” model, combined with other strengths, has enabled China to achieve dominance in multiple strategic sectors, while enhancing its resilience.

proj-syn.title: Which Future for Online Life?
proj-syn.description: By articulating a vision of the future that seems inevitable, technology industry leaders want to create the impression that the surrender of privacy and other defining trends of the current moment cannot be stopped. But predictions become self-fulfilling prophecies only if we believe them and act accordingly.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Legal Tech Funding Down Slightly From All-Time High
crunchbase.description: In the past two years, venture investors have poured more than $7 billion into legal and legal tech startups, most with an AI focus. Funding to the space hit a record level last year, with $4.6 billion invested, per Crunchbase data. So far this year, legal tech startups have pulled in more than $2.2 billion.

crunchbase.title: Inside The Private-Market Divide: EquityZen’s Phil Haslett On AI, SaaS And Secondaries
crunchbase.description: The market for private-company shares has become a much bigger part of the startup ecosystem. In this Crunchbase News Q&A, EquityZen co-founder Phil Haslett discusses why startups are offering employees and investors liquidity earlier, and why secondary prices can be more revealing than headline valuations.

crunchbase.title: Why Bootstrapped Businesses Are More Relevant Than Ever
crunchbase.description: The traditional VC model funds a risky search for product-market fit, argues guest author Richard de Silva of Lateral Investment Management, while bootstrapped founders typically start with known customer problems, prioritize profitability and grow steadily from revenue rather than outside capital.

crunchbase.title: Startups Are Still Acquiring Startups, Led By Ultra-High-Valuation Unicorns
crunchbase.description: Amid fierce competition for an edge in the AI race, well-funded startups commonly find it’s simply faster to buy another company than try to build out certain technologies themselves.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Defense Tech, AI Tools And Infrastructure Lead The Way
crunchbase.description: The biggest financing of the week went to Castelion, a defense tech startup developing a hypersonic missile. Other sizable rounds went to companies developing AI inference technology, a video-creation platform, data centers and voice-to-text tools.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: AI For Everything From Recycling To Breathing To Winning Construction Bids
crunchbase.description: This month’s installment of this column is all AI, though applications for the technology range widely, from two startups that apply AI to trash or recycling, to another that promises to help people breathe and sleep better, to a company that says its AI can help architects and builders spot commercial projects before they’re even announced.

crunchbase.title: From Humanities To AI: How Ali Hussain Built Fintech Tabs Into A $400M Startup
crunchbase.description: Our third in a series of articles about non-tech founders getting venture funding features Tabs founder Ali Hussain, who started the AI fintech after realizing pursuing a Ph.D. in humanities was a terrible idea and spent some time in the tech workforce where he learned a few things about building venture-backed companies.

crunchbase.title: When Should A Board Consider Selling A Company?
crunchbase.description: The best boards continuously evaluate selling alongside scaling, pivoting, or staying independent, especially when the company is thriving, founder priorities are shifting, or strategic buyers begin showing interest, argues tech strategic adviser Itay Sagie. In this guest commentary, he share three signals that tell directors that it’s time to sell the company.

crunchbase.title: Which Investors Have Backed The Most 2026 Unicorns?
crunchbase.description: So far this year, 250 companies have joined the unicorn ranks through Aug. 15, up from 2025's 193 companies. Leading sectors included robotics, AI labs, healthcare and biotech, financial services, AI infrastructure, and AI deployment, among others. But which investors are winning the 2026 funding surge? We take a look.

crunchbase.title: VCs Pour Billions Into Physical AI As The Next Wave Of AI Investing Takes Shape
crunchbase.description: In the first half of 2026, global venture funding in the physical AI space totaled $47.4 billion across 521 deals, per Crunchbase data. That’s up dramatically — almost 4x — compared to the second half of 2025 when startups in the sector raised $12 billion across 470 deals.
